sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and learned HCGP for respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2 who NC: 2024:KHC:50938 is served in this matter, has remained unrepresented before this Court.

3. F.I.R. in Crime No.42/2024 was registered by Huliyar Police Station, Mandya District against the petitioner herein for the aforesaid offences on the basis of first information dated 19.03.2024 received from respondent No.2 herein who is the mother of the victim girl, aged about 16 years.
4. During the course of investigation of the case petitioner herein was arrested on 19.03.2024 and remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation of the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed against him for the aforesaid offences.
Bail application filed by the petitioner before the Sri. Hanumantha @ Hanumesh vs The State Of Karnataka on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/63798233/

sentences.text: 2 Jurisdictional Sessions Court in Crl.Misc.No.1068/2024 was rejected on 27.07.2024.
Therefore, he is before this Court.

5. Learned Counsel for the petitioner having reiterated the grounds urged in this petition submits that NC: 2024:KHC:50938 petitioner is a youngster having no criminal antecedents, he and the victim girl were in love.
Investigation of the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.

The victim girl has been already examined before the Trial Court as P.W-1 and therefore, there cannot be any apprehension that petitioner is likely to tamper with the material charge sheet witness in the present case.
Accordingly, he prays to allow this petition.
6. Per contra, learned HCGP has opposed the petition.

He submits that victim girl has supported the case of the prosecution and the DNA test report would go to show that the petitioner is the biological father of the product of conception sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory.
Accordingly he prays to dismiss this petition.

7. Perusal of the first information and the charge sheet filed in the present case would go to show that on 06.01.2024, the victim girl and her friend had gone to their school to attend the school day function.

After the school day function was over, petitioner on the guise of NC: 2024:KHC:50938 dropping the victim girl and her friend had taken the victim girl to his house after dropping her friend near her house.

It is alleged that the petitioner who had taken the victim girl to his house,
allegedly had sexually assaulted her against her wishes and thereafter, threatened her with dire consequences in the event she reveals the act committed by him to anybody.

It appears that the victim girl had subsequently missed her periods and therefore she was taken to the hospital for medical checkup and in the hospital the Doctor had informed the parents of the victim girl that she was pregnant.

Thereafter, the victim girl had approached the police on 19.03.2024 and based on the first information submitted by the mother of the victim girl, FIR has been registered against the petitioner for the aforesaid offences.
Petitioner aged about 19 years having no criminal antecedents was arrested in the present case on 19.03.2024 and subsequently, remanded to judicial custody.
Investigation of the case is completed and charge sheet has been filed.

Victim girl has been completely examined before the Trial Court as P.W-1 and NC: 2024:KHC:50938 therefore as rightly contended by learned Counsel for the petitioner there cannot be any apprehension that the petitioner is likely to tamper with the material charge sheet witness.
Prosecution in all has cited 30 charge sheet witnesses in the present case.
Till today, only one charge sheet witness has been examined.
Therefore, the chances of trial being completed and the case being disposed off on merits in the near soon is very remote.

Considering the aforesaid aspects of the matter and also having regard to the age of the petitioner who has no other criminal antecedents, I am of the view that,
without expressing any opinion on the merits and demerits of the case, the prayer made by the petitioner for grant of regular bail needs to be answered affirmatively.

Accordingly, the following:-
ORDER
The petition is allowed.
